passages.text: Now when Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he was furious and filled with indignation. He ridiculed the Jews before his associates and the army of Samaria, saying, “What are these feeble Jews doing? Can they restore the wall by themselves? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they complete it in a day? Can they bring these burnt stones back to life from the mounds of rubble?”
passages.sermon:
Sanballat was a leader who opposed the Jews.
He heard that we were rebuilding the wall.
He became very angry.
He was filled with indignation.
He mocked the Jews.
He did this in front of his associates.
He did this in front of the army of Samaria.
He said, “What are these weak Jews doing?”
He asked, “Can they restore the wall by themselves?”
He asked, “Will they offer sacrifices?”
He asked, “Will they finish it in a day?”
He asked, “Can they bring these burnt stones back to life from the piles of rubble?”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֞י כַּאֲשֶׁ֧ר שָׁמַ֣ע סַנְבַלַּ֗ט כִּֽי־ אֲנַ֤חְנוּ בוֹנִים֙ אֶת־ הַ֣חוֹמָ֔ה וַיִּ֣חַר ל֔וֹ וַיִּכְעַ֖ס הַרְבֵּ֑ה וַיַּלְעֵ֖ג עַל־ הַיְּהוּדִֽים׃ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀ לִפְנֵ֣י אֶחָ֗יו וְחֵיל֙ שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מָ֛ה הַיְּהוּדִ֥ים הָאֲמֵלָלִ֖ים עֹשִׂ֑ים הֲיַעַזְב֨וּ לָהֶ֤ם הֲיִזְבָּ֙חוּ֙ הַיְכַלּ֣וּ בַיּ֔וֹם הַיְחַיּ֧וּ אֶת־ הָאֲבָנִ֛ים מֵעֲרֵמ֥וֹת הֶעָפָ֖ר וְהֵ֥מָּה שְׂרוּפֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Then Tobiah the Ammonite, who was beside him, said, “If even a fox were to climb up on what they are building, it would break down their wall of stones!”
passages.sermon:
Tobiah was an Ammonite.
Tobiah stood beside Sanballat.
Tobiah spoke about the Jews and their work.
Tobiah said the Jews were building a wall of stones.
Tobiah said, “If even a fox climbs up on their wall, it will break it down.”
Tobiah meant the wall was weak.
passages.original: וְטוֹבִיָּ֥ה הָעַמֹּנִ֖י אֶצְל֑וֹ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר גַּ֚ם אֲשֶׁר־ הֵ֣ם בּוֹנִ֔ים אִם־ יַעֲלֶ֣ה שׁוּעָ֔ל וּפָרַ֖ץ חוֹמַ֥ת אַבְנֵיהֶֽם׃פ

passages.text: Hear us, O God, for we are despised. Turn their scorn back upon their own heads, and let them be taken as plunder to a land of captivity.
passages.sermon:
God, you are our God.
We are despised.
Hear us.
Our enemies mock us.
Return their shame onto themselves.
Let them become plunder.
Send them to a land of captivity.
passages.original: שְׁמַ֤ע אֱלֹהֵ֙ינוּ֙ כִּֽי־ הָיִ֣ינוּ בוּזָ֔ה וְהָשֵׁ֥ב חֶרְפָּתָ֖ם אֶל־ רֹאשָׁ֑ם וּתְנֵ֥ם לְבִזָּ֖ה בְּאֶ֥רֶץ שִׁבְיָֽה׃

passages.text: Do not cover up their iniquity or let their sin be blotted out from Your sight, for they have provoked the builders.
passages.sermon:
God, do not hide their wrongdoing.
Do not erase their sin from Your sight.
They have angered the builders.
They have acted against those rebuilding the wall.
passages.original: וְאַל־ תְּכַס֙ עַל־ עֲוֺנָ֔ם וְחַטָּאתָ֖ם מִלְּפָנֶ֣יךָ אַל־ תִּמָּחֶ֑ה כִּ֥י הִכְעִ֖יסוּ לְנֶ֥גֶד הַבּוֹנִֽים׃

passages.text: So we rebuilt the wall until all of it was joined together up to half its height, for the people had a mind to work.
passages.sermon:
The people of Jerusalem rebuilt the wall.
They joined the entire wall together.
They built it up to half its height.
The people wanted to work.
They were determined to finish the wall.
passages.original: וַנִּבְנֶה֙ אֶת־ הַ֣חוֹמָ֔ה וַתִּקָּשֵׁ֥ר כָּל־ הַחוֹמָ֖ה עַד־ חֶצְיָ֑הּ וַיְהִ֧י לֵ֦ב לָעָ֖ם לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃פ

passages.text: When Sanballat and Tobiah, together with the Arabs, Ammonites, and Ashdodites, heard that the repair to the walls of Jerusalem was progressing and that the gaps were being closed, they were furious, and all of them conspired to come and fight against Jerusalem and create a hindrance.
passages.sermon:
Sanballat was an enemy of the Jews.
Tobiah was also an enemy of the Jews.
The Arabs, Ammonites, and Ashdodites were enemies too.
They heard news about Jerusalem.
They learned that the walls of Jerusalem were being repaired.
They saw that the gaps in the wall were being closed.
This progress made them very angry.
All these enemies joined together.
They made a plan to come to Jerusalem.
They wanted to fight against Jerusalem.
They wanted to cause confusion and stop the work.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י כַאֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁמַ֣ע סַנְבַלַּ֡ט וְ֠טוֹבִיָּה וְהָעַרְבִ֨ים וְהָעַמֹּנִ֜ים וְהָאַשְׁדּוֹדִ֗ים כִּֽי־ עָלְתָ֤ה אֲרוּכָה֙ לְחֹמ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם כִּי־ הֵחֵ֥לּוּ הַפְּרֻצִ֖ים לְהִסָּתֵ֑ם וַיִּ֥חַר לָהֶ֖ם מְאֹֽד׃ וַיִּקְשְׁר֤וּ כֻלָּם֙ יַחְדָּ֔ו לָב֖וֹא לְהִלָּחֵ֣ם בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְלַעֲשׂ֥וֹת ל֖וֹ תּוֹעָֽה׃

passages.text: So we prayed to our God and posted a guard against them day and night.
passages.sermon:
The people of Jerusalem faced enemies who wanted to attack them.
They prayed to their God.
They asked God for help.
They also took action.
They posted a guard to watch for danger.
They kept the guard on duty during the day.
They kept the guard on duty during the night.
They did this to protect themselves from their enemies.
passages.original: וַנִּתְפַּלֵּ֖ל אֶל־ אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וַנַּעֲמִ֨יד מִשְׁמָ֧ר עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם יוֹמָ֥ם וָלַ֖יְלָה מִפְּנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Meanwhile, the people of Judah said: “The strength of the laborer fails, and there is so much rubble that we will never be able to rebuild the wall.”
passages.sermon:
The people of Judah spoke.
They said the workers are losing strength.
They said there is too much rubble.
They said we cannot rebuild the wall.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוּדָ֗ה כָּשַׁל֙ כֹּ֣חַ הַסַּבָּ֔ל וְהֶעָפָ֖ר הַרְבֵּ֑ה וַאֲנַ֙חְנוּ֙ לֹ֣א נוּכַ֔ל לִבְנ֖וֹת בַּחוֹמָֽה׃

passages.text: And our enemies said, “Before they know or see a thing, we will come into their midst, kill them, and put an end to the work.”
passages.sermon:
Our enemies spoke.
They made a plan.
They said, “The people will not know.
They will not see us.
We will come into their midst.
We will kill them.
We will stop the work.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ צָרֵ֗ינוּ לֹ֤א יֵדְעוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א יִרְא֔וּ עַ֛ד אֲשֶׁר־ נָב֥וֹא אֶל־ תּוֹכָ֖ם וַהֲרַגְנ֑וּם וְהִשְׁבַּ֖תְנוּ אֶת־ הַמְּלָאכָֽה׃

passages.text: At that time the Jews who lived nearby came and told us ten times over, “Wherever you turn, they will attack us.”
passages.sermon:
The Jews lived near our enemies.
These Jews came to us.
They warned us many times.
They told us this warning ten times.
They said, “Wherever you turn, they will attack us.”
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ כַּאֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֣אוּ הַיְּהוּדִ֔ים הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים אֶצְלָ֑ם וַיֹּ֤אמְרוּ לָ֙נוּ֙ עֶ֣שֶׂר פְּעָמִ֔ים מִכָּל־ הַמְּקֹמ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁר־ תָּשׁ֥וּבוּ עָלֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: So I stationed men behind the lowest sections of the wall, at the vulnerable areas. I stationed them by families with their swords, spears, and bows.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah led the people of Jerusalem.
Their enemies threatened to attack them.
Nehemiah took action to protect the people.
He placed men behind the lowest parts of the city wall.
These were the most vulnerable places.
He grouped the men by their families.
Each family stood together.
They held swords.
They held spears.
They held bows.
They were ready to defend the city.
passages.original: וָֽאַעֲמִ֞יד מִֽתַּחְתִּיּ֧וֹת לַמָּק֛וֹם מֵאַחֲרֵ֥י לַחוֹמָ֖ה בַּצְּחִחִיִּים וָֽאַעֲמִ֤יד אֶת־ הָעָם֙ לְמִשְׁפָּח֔וֹת עִם־ חַרְבֹתֵיהֶ֛ם רָמְחֵיהֶ֖ם וְקַשְּׁתֹתֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: After I had made an inspection, I stood up and said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, “Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons and your daughters, your wives and your homes.”
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was the leader of the Jews rebuilding Jerusalem’s wall.
He inspected the situation.
He stood up.
He spoke to the nobles.
He spoke to the officials.
He spoke to the rest of the people.
He said, “Do not be afraid of your enemies.”
He said, “Remember the Lord.”
The Lord is great.
The Lord is awesome.
He said, “Fight for your brothers.”
He said, “Fight for your sons.”
He said, “Fight for your daughters.”
He said, “Fight for your wives.”
He said, “Fight for your homes.”
passages.original: וָאֵ֣רֶא וָאָק֗וּם וָאֹמַ֞ר אֶל־ הַחֹרִ֤ים וְאֶל־ הַסְּגָנִים֙ וְאֶל־ יֶ֣תֶר הָעָ֔ם אַל־ תִּֽירְא֖וּ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם אֶת־ אֲדֹנָ֞י הַגָּד֤וֹל וְהַנּוֹרָא֙ זְכֹ֔רוּ וְהִֽלָּחֲמ֗וּ עַל־ אֲחֵיכֶם֙ בְּנֵיכֶ֣ם וּבְנֹתֵיכֶ֔ם נְשֵׁיכֶ֖ם וּבָתֵּיכֶֽם׃פ

passages.text: When our enemies heard that we were aware of their scheme and that God had frustrated it, each of us returned to his own work on the wall.
passages.sermon:
Our enemies made a plan against us.
We learned about their plan.
God stopped their plan.
Our enemies heard that we knew about their plan.
They also heard that God had stopped it.
Then each of us went back to the wall.
Each person returned to his own work.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֞י כַּֽאֲשֶׁר־ שָׁמְע֤וּ אוֹיְבֵ֙ינוּ֙ כִּי־ נ֣וֹדַֽע לָ֔נוּ וַיָּ֥פֶר הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־ עֲצָתָ֑ם וַנָּשׁוּב כֻּלָּ֙נוּ֙ אֶל־ הַ֣חוֹמָ֔ה אִ֖ישׁ אֶל־ מְלַאכְתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And from that day on, half of my servants did the work while the other half held spears, shields, bows, and armor. The officers stationed themselves behind all the people of Judah who were rebuilding the wall. The laborers who carried materials worked with one hand and held a weapon with the other.
passages.sermon:
From that day on, I divided my servants into two groups.
Half of my servants worked on the construction.
The other half held spears, shields, bows, and armor.
The officers stood behind all the people of Judah.
The people of Judah were rebuilding the wall.
The laborers carried materials for the work.
Each laborer used one hand to do the work.
Each laborer held a weapon in the other hand.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ מִן־ הַיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא חֲצִ֣י נְעָרַי֮ עֹשִׂ֣ים בַּמְּלָאכָה֒ וְחֶצְיָ֗ם מַחֲזִיקִים֙ וְהָרְמָחִ֣ים הַמָּגִנִּ֔ים וְהַקְּשָׁת֖וֹת וְהַשִּׁרְיֹנִ֑ים וְהַ֨שָּׂרִ֔ים אַחֲרֵ֖י כָּל־ בֵּ֥ית יְהוּדָֽה׃ הַבּוֹנִ֧ים בַּחוֹמָ֛ה וְהַנֹּשְׂאִ֥ים בַּסֶּ֖בֶל עֹמְשִׂ֑ים בְּאַחַ֤ת יָדוֹ֙ עֹשֶׂ֣ה בַמְּלָאכָ֔ה וְאַחַ֖ת מַחֲזֶ֥קֶת הַשָּֽׁלַח׃

passages.text: And each of the builders worked with his sword strapped at his side. But the trumpeter stayed beside me.
passages.sermon: The builders worked on the wall.\r\nEach builder kept his sword strapped at his side.\r\nThe trumpeter stood next to me.
passages.original: וְהַ֨בּוֹנִ֔ים אִ֥ישׁ חַרְבּ֛וֹ אֲסוּרִ֥ים עַל־ מָתְנָ֖יו וּבוֹנִ֑ים וְהַתּוֹקֵ֥עַ בַּשּׁוֹפָ֖ר אֶצְלִֽי׃

passages.text: Then I said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people: “The work is great and extensive, and we are spread out far from one another along the wall.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah spoke to the nobles.
He spoke to the officials.
He spoke to the rest of the people.
He said the work is great.
He said the work is extensive.
He said, “We are spread out along the wall.”
He said, “Each person is far from his brother.”
passages.original: וָאֹמַ֞ר אֶל־ הַחֹרִ֤ים וְאֶל־ הַסְּגָנִים֙ וְאֶל־ יֶ֣תֶר הָעָ֔ם הַמְּלָאכָ֥ה הַרְבֵּ֖ה וּרְחָבָ֑ה וַאֲנַ֗חְנוּ נִפְרָדִים֙ עַל־ הַ֣חוֹמָ֔ה רְחוֹקִ֖ים אִ֥ישׁ מֵאָחִֽיו׃

passages.text: Wherever you hear the sound of the horn, rally to us there. Our God will fight for us!”
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel rebuilt Jerusalem’s wall.
They worked while enemies threatened them.
Nehemiah led them.
He spoke to the people.
He said, “Listen for the sound of the horn.
If you hear the horn, go to that place.
Gather with us there.
Our God will fight for us.”
passages.original: בִּמְק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר תִּשְׁמְעוּ֙ אֶת־ ק֣וֹל הַשּׁוֹפָ֔ר שָׁ֖מָּה תִּקָּבְצ֣וּ אֵלֵ֑ינוּ אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ יִלָּ֥חֶם לָֽנוּ׃

passages.text: So we continued the work, while half of the men held spears from the break of dawn until the stars came out.
passages.sermon: We worked on the task.\r\nHalf of the men held spears.\r\nThey held spears from dawn until the stars appeared.
passages.original: וַאֲנַ֖חְנוּ עֹשִׂ֣ים בַּמְּלָאכָ֑ה וְחֶצְיָ֗ם מַחֲזִיקִים֙ בָּֽרְמָחִ֔ים מֵעֲל֣וֹת הַשַּׁ֔חַר עַ֖ד צֵ֥את הַכּוֹכָבִֽים׃

passages.text: At that time I also said to the people, “Let every man and his servant spend the night inside Jerusalem, so that they can stand guard by night and work by day.”
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was the leader of the people rebuilding Jerusalem’s walls.
At that time, I spoke to the people.
I said, “Every man must stay inside Jerusalem at night.
Each man’s servant must also stay inside Jerusalem at night.
You must do this so we can guard the city at night.
You must also do this so we can work during the day.”
passages.original: גַּ֣ם בָּעֵ֤ת הַהִיא֙ אָמַ֣רְתִּי לָעָ֔ם אִ֣ישׁ וְנַעֲר֔וֹ יָלִ֖ינוּ בְּת֣וֹךְ יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְהָֽיוּ־ לָ֧נוּ הַלַּ֛יְלָה מִשְׁמָ֖ר וְהַיּ֥וֹם מְלָאכָֽה׃

passages.text: So neither I nor my brothers nor my servants nor the guards with me changed out of our clothes; each carried his weapon, even to go for water.
passages.sermon:
I am Nehemiah.
My brothers, my servants, and the guards with me worked with me.
None of us took off our clothes.
Each man kept his weapon with him.
Each man carried his weapon even when he went for water.
passages.original: וְאֵ֨ין אֲנִ֜י וְאַחַ֣י וּנְעָרַ֗י וְאַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמִּשְׁמָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַחֲרַ֔י אֵין־ אֲנַ֥חְנוּ פֹשְׁטִ֖ים בְּגָדֵ֑ינוּ אִ֖ישׁ שִׁלְח֥וֹ הַמָּֽיִם׃ס
